correctness.rationale: For each integer m≥1, F_m(s)=(1−s)(s+s^(−1))^(m−1)−s² has a unique root on (0,1): the ratio (1−s)(s+s^(−1))^(m−1)/s² strictly decreases from infinity to zero. Put λ=s+s^(−1), c=1/(λ−2), h(j)=λ^j for j<m and c+(λ^m−c)s^(j−m) for j≥m, with h(∞)=c. The root equation is equivalent to the interface relation λ^m−c=s(λ^(m−1)−c). Using s+s^(−1)=λ and (λ−2)c=1 verifies Mh=λh at every j and at infinity. The identity c/λ^m=1/[(1−s)(1+s²)]>1 gives 1≤h≤c and positivity; order bounds give r(M)=λ exactly. Writing M=S+K with (Sf)(j)=f(j−1)+f(j+1) for j≥m, S(∞)=2f(∞), S(j<m)=0 gives norm S≤2 and finite-rank K. Hence normalized T=M/λ is quasi-compact (distance ≤2/λ<1 to compact K/λ). Uniform common occurrence of each isolated letter after sufficiently many iterates proves primitivity, so MRW Theorem 6.7 implies minimality and unique ergodicity. The defining root gives δ=1−s=2^(1−m)(1+O(2^(−m))) and λ−2=δ²/s=4^(1−m)(1+O(2^(−m))). The λ^n/c≤|ρ_m^n(0)|≤λ^n bound and exact rational binomial certificate yield the 72000-step crossing at m=7; the 1000-step below-two bound was independently recomputed. Direct independent script checked m=1..16 high-precision eigenfunction residuals, exact finite length 2-stall at n=34, the 7-stall n=1000 bound, and exact rational 72000 binomial bound; none substitutes for the universal proof.

value.rationale: The result classifies a natural, explicitly studied family of nearest-neighbor compact-alphabet substitutions for every finite stall, resolving a reported seven-stall negative prediction in the opposite direction by a rigorously positive spectral gap. A sharp exponentially small λ_m−2 law mathematically explains a long misleading finite transient, and a rational certificate supplies an explicit cutoff witnessing reversal. Unlike routine PF substitution, the noncompact countable alphabet requires an explicit positive eigenfunction, spectral bound and compact perturbation; the full all-m classification is independently useful and motivated by an existing open spectral question. Limitations to this tail rule and finite stalls are appropriately stated.
